summary.text: Andrew Gounardes is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent seeking re-election to State Senate District 26 in Brooklyn. A Brooklyn-born lawyer and former aide to local officials, he lost a 2012 Senate race, won the seat in 2018, and has represented District 26 since redistricting in 2023. He chairs the Senate Budget and Revenue Committee and has sponsored legislation on AI safety, social media regulation for minors, tax credits for families, and immigration protections.

paragraphs.text: Andrew Gounardes was born in Brooklyn and raised in Bay Ridge, according to Wikipedia, and he graduated from Fort Hamilton High School.
He earned a B.A. in political science from Hunter College in 2006 and a J.D. from George Washington University Law School in 2010.

He worked as an attorney, as counsel to the Brooklyn Borough President, as director of external affairs for the Citizens Committee for New York City, and as a staff assistant in the U.S. Senate before entering elected office.

His Senate biography says he began in public service as an aide to City Councilmember Vincent Gentile and served as counsel to Brooklyn Borough President Eric Adams for five years, and that he later served as a trustee of the New York City Employees' Retirement System and, after Superstorm Sandy, co-founded the nonprofit Bay Ridge Cares.
Gounardes ran for State Senate District 22 in 2012 on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines and lost to incumbent Republican Martin Golden.
He defeated Golden in the November 2018 general election to win the District 22 seat and took office in January 2019, and he has represented District 26 since 2023.

In the 2025-2026 session he chairs the Senate Budget and Revenue Committee and also sits on the Judiciary, Codes, Finance, Higher Education, Insurance, Ethics and Internal Governance, and Internet and Technology committees.

According to his campaign website, he has written more than 100 laws since taking office and is the father of three young children; his stated priorities include online safety for children, universal child care, and transit and street safety.
